mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns despite a decline in UNRATE, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.5% may signal monetary tightening, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong economic demand, which may boost corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 and HOUST both increase but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during a late-cycle expansion signals that supply chains are meeting demand, which may lead to sustained economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases in a late-cycle expansion but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains low but the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 50,000 in one month
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 50,000 but the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand across multiple sectors, which may drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS and HOUST both increase but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary tightening cycle may increase borrowing costs and reduce investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises during a tightening cycle but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns, this hypothesis is rejected.
